# SQL

Duration: 4 months / 16 teaching weeks.
Schedule: 6 instructor-led hours weekly (96 total), plus 4 to 6 independent study hours.

Progress through beginner, intermediate, and advanced SQL skills, then apply them to a layered data warehouse and analytical projects. The course covers query design, reusable objects, performance analysis, and validated business reporting.

## Prerequisites

Basic computer literacy and spreadsheet familiarity. No previous programming required.

## Tools

SQL Server Developer Edition or an institution-approved SQL sandbox; SQL Server Management Studio; Git.

## Learning outcomes

- Query and modify relational data using SELECT, DDL, DML, filtering, joins, and set operators.
- Apply scalar, aggregate, CASE, NULL, and window functions to business analysis.
- Choose subqueries, CTEs, views, temporary tables, procedures, and triggers for appropriate use cases.
- Evaluate indexes, execution plans, partitioning, and optimization decisions; validate AI-assisted SQL.
- Build Bronze, Silver, and Gold warehouse layers and deliver exploratory and advanced analytics.

## Weekly schedule

### Week 1 — SQL foundations

Introduction to SQL, environment setup and querying data with SELECT.

Practical: Set up the database and produce basic business queries.

### Week 2 — DDL and DML

CREATE, ALTER and DROP; INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE; constraints.

Practical: Create tables and demonstrate controlled data changes.

### Week 3 — Filtering and joins

Filtering data, basic joins, unmatched rows and cardinality.

Practical: Combine customer and order records without inflating totals.

### Week 4 — Advanced joins and sets

Advanced joins, anti/semi join patterns and set operators.

Practical: Compare populations and identify missing or duplicate records.

### Week 5 — Scalar functions

SQL functions overview; string, numeric, date and time functions.

Practical: Standardize names, calculate values and validate date logic.

### Week 6 — NULL and aggregation

NULL functions, CASE, aggregate functions and grouping.

Practical: Produce reconciled segmented KPIs with explicit missing-value rules.

### Week 7 — Window functions

Window basics, aggregate, ranking and value functions; frames.

Practical: Calculate rankings, running totals and prior-period comparisons.

### Week 8 — Midpoint practical

Beginner and intermediate skills; query validation and troubleshooting.

Practical: Complete an independent reporting and data-quality exercise.

### Week 9 — Subqueries and CTEs

Advanced techniques, subqueries, common table expressions.

Practical: Refactor a multi-step query and verify equivalent results.

### Week 10 — Views and intermediate tables

Views, CTAS, temporary tables and comparison of techniques.

Practical: Choose and implement a suitable intermediate-results strategy.

### Week 11 — Procedures and triggers

Stored procedures, parameters, triggers and operational side effects.

Practical: Build a parameterized report and a narrowly scoped audit trigger.

### Week 12 — Performance and AI

Indexes, execution plans, partitions, optimization tips; AI and SQL.

Practical: Compare plans, justify an optimization and validate an AI-suggested query.

### Week 13 — Data warehouse Bronze

Warehouse architecture, source ingestion, raw preservation and lineage.

Practical: Build the Bronze layer and reconcile it with source files.

### Week 14 — Data warehouse Silver

Cleaning, standardization, deduplication and quality checks.

Practical: Build the Silver layer with documented transformation rules.

### Week 15 — Data warehouse Gold and EDA

Dimensional modeling, reporting views and exploratory data analysis.

Practical: Build Gold outputs and investigate distributions and anomalies.

### Week 16 — Advanced analytics and defense

Customer and product segmentation, trends, cumulative metrics and handover.

Practical: Present advanced analytics backed by a validated warehouse.

## Capstone

SQL data warehouse and business analytics portfolio

Submit source ingestion scripts, Bronze raw tables, Silver cleaned tables, a Gold dimensional model or analytical views, data quality checks, EDA queries, advanced analytics queries, and a README. Include an execution-plan comparison, a parameterized procedure, and a scoped trigger demonstration.

## Assessment

- Weekly practical work: 25%
- Knowledge checks: 10%
- Midpoint practical: 20%
- Capstone artifact: 35%
- Presentation and defense: 10%
